# GearGo: System Design

GearGo is a web app for a small equipment-rental business that rents camping gear, power tools and event equipment. Customers browse equipment and request rentals. Staff and managers run the business.

---

## 1. Problem Statement

**The problem:** There is no single place to see what equipment is available and ask to rent it. Requests are assumed to be handled by phone, messages or spreadsheets, so staff check stock by hand and items can be double-booked. *(Assumption: confirm with the business owner.)*

**Who is affected:**

- **Customers** cannot see availability or prices without contacting the business.
- **Staff** waste time answering availability questions and keeping manual records.
- **Managers** have no clear view of the catalogue, demand or users.

**Business impact:** lost bookings, double-booked items, wasted staff time, and no data on which items are popular.

**Proposed solution:** a web app where customers browse and request rentals, staff process requests and manage equipment, and managers manage the catalogue and users.

**Solution boundary (version 1):**

| Included | Not included |
|---|---|
| Register and log in (by role) | Online payments |
| Browse and search equipment | Delivery |
| Submit and cancel rental requests | Damage and insurance |
| Staff approve, reject and track rentals | Invoicing |
| Manager control of catalogue and users | Mobile app |

---

## 2. User Roles

| Role | Who | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| **Customer** | Someone who wants to rent equipment | Browse equipment, submit and track their own requests |
| **Staff** | Employee running daily rentals | Everything a customer can do, plus manage equipment and process all requests |
| **Manager** | Owner or supervisor | Everything staff can do, plus manage users, roles and the catalogue |

---

## 3. Use Cases

A use case is one thing a user wants to do in the system.

**Customer**

- UC-C1: Register / log in
- UC-C2: Browse and search equipment
- UC-C3: View equipment details
- UC-C4: Submit a rental request
- UC-C5: View and cancel my own requests

**Staff**

- UC-S1: Log in
- UC-S2: Add and edit equipment
- UC-S3: Update equipment availability
- UC-S4: Review rental requests
- UC-S5: Approve or reject a request
- UC-S6: Record collection and return

**Manager**

- UC-M1: Manage user accounts
- UC-M2: Assign roles
- UC-M3: Manage the catalogue
- UC-M4: Override (cancel or change) any request
- UC-M5: View rental overview

A Manager can also do every Staff use case.

## 5. MVC Architecture Sketch

![MVC architecture sketch: Browser to Controller to Service to Data Access to Database, with the response returning through the View](data:image/png;base64,)

**Browser → Controller → Service / Business Logic → Data Access → Database**

| Layer | Its job |
|---|---|
| Browser | Shows pages and sends requests |
| Controller | Receives the request and decides what to do |
| Service / Business Logic | Applies the rules (for example, no overlapping bookings) |
| Data Access | Reads and writes the database |
| Database | Stores the data |
| View | Builds the page sent back to the browser |

---

## 6. First ERD

![ERD with the User, Equipment and RentalRequest tables](data:image/png;base64,)

**Tables:** User, Equipment, RentalRequest. Customers, staff and managers share the User table and are told apart by a Role column.

**Relationships:**

- One User submits many RentalRequests.
- One Equipment item appears in many RentalRequests.
- One User (staff or manager) reviews many RentalRequests.

**Request status:** Pending → Approved → Collected → Returned. A request can also be Rejected or Cancelled.

**Keys:** PK = primary key (identifies a row). FK = foreign key (points to a row in another table).

**Limitation:** one request covers one equipment type. A later version could add a RentalRequestItem table to allow several items per request.
